dek: Collider ranked the best TV since 2000, from Breaking Bad to Fleabag.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: Collider ranked the *6 best shows* released between 2000 and today. No theme, just pure greatness.

slides.label: Better Call Saul
slides.text: At #6: Jimmy McGill (Bob Odenkirk) can do honest work, but keeps reaching for *the shortcut* instead (2015-2022).

slides.label: Fleabag
slides.text: At #5: *Fleabag* (Phoebe Waller-Bridge) jokes straight to camera to dodge grief she can't say out loud (2016-2019).

slides.label: Succession
slides.text: At #4: Logan Roy's (Brian Cox) kids plan his succession in the hospital, then he recovers and *keeps them guessing* (2018-2023).

slides.label: Mad Men
slides.text: At #3: Don Draper (Jon Hamm) sells America's deepest feelings in ads, but *can't be honest at home* (2007-2015).

slides.label: The Wire
slides.text: At #2: Detective Jimmy McNulty (Dominic West) chases Baltimore's drug trade while bosses want him to *stop* (2002-2008).

slides.label: Breaking Bad
slides.text: At #1: Walter White (Bryan Cranston) cooks meth for his family's future, then *can't stop* even after he's rich (2008-2013).

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: Great TV gives complicated people room to be flawed and full, the same respect underrepresented stories deserve.

caption_instagram: Collider just ranked the 6 best shows released from 2000 to now, and the list runs from Breaking Bad to Fleabag to The Wire. Walter White's chemistry-meets-crime arc tops the ranking, with Succession's Roy family drama, Mad Men's Don Draper, Better Call Saul's Jimmy McGill, and The Wire's Baltimore drug war rounding out the top tier. Great TV doesn't ask you to like these people, it asks you to understand them. Jimmy, Walt, Fleabag, Shiv, they're all reaching for something and getting in their own way. That's the same messy humanity underrepresented creators are fighting to put on screen, not polished, just real. Which show tops your list? One name. caption_linkedin:
Collider just ranked the 6 best television shows released between 2000 and now, and the list (Breaking Bad, The Wire, Mad Men, Succession, Fleabag, Better Call Saul) offers a clear lesson for anyone building an audience. None of these shows lead with a hook and coast. They build characters worth arguing about over years, then let the tension pay off slowly. Walter White's turn, Jimmy McGill's shortcuts, Shiv Roy's loyalty tests all took seasons to earn. For founders and creators building a brand or a following, the takeaway is patience. Audiences don't just want a clean pitch, they want someone they can watch change, mess up, and keep showing up. That's as true for a newsletter as it is for prestige TV. Which show tops your list? One name. #TheInnovatorsDen #Storytelling #ContentStrategy
